items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: And Mutt Carey was very good for that, and Buddy Petit.

ctx.x: And Mutt Carey was very good for that, and Buddy Petit.

Well, let's say that today was the day that we worked out for the first time in Maryland, my Maryland, and then you worked out the parts that you were going to play, and you'd probably play five or six choruses, the band would total, seven or eight choruses, and you had that all worked out. When you started playing it, would you play the same notes pretty much every time in the weeks and the months as they went by? That you worked out that first day in Maryland? That trombone solo? Well, no, not just the solo,…

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: Buddy told him I had too much weight for him. He said, you know what job he got on the riverfront? He said, my band had too much weight for him.

ctx.x: Could you give me that picture of Thomas' man?

Buddy, I didn't get rid of Buddy. Buddy got ready to set. Buddy told him I had too much weight for him. He said, you know what job he got on the riverfront? He said, my band had too much weight for him. I guess he wanted to set up his own band. That's all I feel.
Can you find me a picture of Louie Nelson, the trombone player? Over there in the files, he doesn't show in this one.
